notes:
### 1. Individual Income Tax Rate(s) & Brackets

Rhode Island imposes an individual income tax with three graduated tax brackets under a uniform rate schedule applicable to all filing statuses (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-30-2.6). The bracket thresholds are adjusted annually for inflation:

* **Tax Year 2025:**
  * Over $0 to $79,900: **3.75%**
  * Over $79,900 to $181,650: **$2,996.25 + 4.75%** of the amount over $79,900
  * Over $181,650: **$7,829.38 + 5.99%** of the amount over $181,650
  * *Standard Deduction (2025):* Single / Married Filing Separately: $10,900; Married Filing Jointly: $21,800; Head of Household: $16,350. Personal Exemption: $5,100.

* **Tax Year 2026 (Adjusted for inflation):**
  * Over $0 to $82,050: **3.75%**
  * Over $82,050 to $186,450: **$3,076.88 + 4.75%** of the amount over $82,050
  * Over $186,450: **$8,035.88 + 5.99%** of the amount over $186,450
  * *Standard Deduction (2026):* Single / Married Filing Separately: $11,200; Married Filing Jointly: $22,400; Head of Household: $16,800. Personal Exemption: $5,250.

* **Official URLs:**
  * Advisory ADV 2024-26 (Tax Year 2025) & ADV 2025-22 (Tax Year 2026): https://tax.ri.gov/guidance/advisories
  * Personal Income Tax: https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/personal-income-tax

---

### 2. Corporate Income / Franchise Tax Rate(s) & Minimum Tax

* **Corporate Income Tax Rate:** **7%** (7.00%) of Rhode Island taxable income (applies to both Tax Year 2025 and Tax Year 2026; unchanged).
* **Minimum Tax:** **$400** per corporation (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-11-2(e)).
* **Other Business Entities Subject to Minimum Tax/Fee:**
  * S-corporations are subject to the corporate minimum tax of **$400** (plus the 7% tax on any federal taxable income).
  * Limited liability companies (LLCs), limited partnerships (LPs), limited liability partnerships (LLPs), and single-member LLCs (SMLLCs) not taxed as corporations federally are subject to an annual filing charge/fee equal to the corporate minimum tax of **$400** (General partnerships are exempt from this fee).
* **Franchise Tax:** Repealed effective January 1, 2015 (previously under R.I. Gen. Laws Chapter 44-12). It does not apply to tax years 2025 or 2026.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax/tax-filing-requirements
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax/pass-through-entities

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax Rate & Local Rates

* **State Sales and Use Tax Rate:** **7%** (0.07) imposed on the retail sale, rental, lease, storage, use, or consumption of taxable tangible personal property and enumerated services (applies to both Tax Year 2025 and Tax Year 2026; unchanged).
* **Local Jurisdictions Rate Additions:**
  * **General Sales Tax:** Local jurisdictions (cities and towns) do **not** add local general sales taxes. The 7% rate is uniform statewide.
  * **Special Industry-Specific Local Taxes:**
    * **Meals & Beverage Tax:** Eating and drinking establishments must collect an additional **1%** local meals and beverage tax on taxable sales of meals and beverages, making the total rate **8%**.
    * **Local Hotel Tax:** Lodging facilities collect a local hotel tax (1% in 2025, increasing to 2% effective January 1, 2026 for short-term rentals and hotels) in addition to state hotel tax and the 7% sales tax.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/sales-excise-taxes/sales-use-tax
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/sales-excise-taxes/meals-beverage-tax

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes

* **General Gross Receipts / Margin Tax:** Rhode Island does not impose a general statewide business gross receipts, gross margin, or franchise tax.
* **Franchise Tax:** Officially repealed as of January 1, 2015.
* **Notable Specific Business Gross Earnings & Entity Taxes (applicable to 2025 and 2026):**
  * **Public Service Corporation Gross Earnings Tax (Form T-72, R.I. Gen. Laws Chapter 44-13):** Imposed on gross earnings of public utilities, cable, and telecommunications companies (e.g., 5% on telecommunications gross earnings).
  * **Bank Excise Tax (Form T-74, R.I. Gen. Laws Chapter 44-14):** Imposed on banking institutions at **9%** of net income (minimum tax of $100).
  * **Insurance Gross Premiums Tax (Form T-71, R.I. Gen. Laws Chapter 44-17):** Imposed on insurance companies at **2%** of gross premiums.
  * **Pass-Through Entity Election Tax (Schedule PTE, R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-11-2.3):** Elective entity-level tax for pass-through entities at a flat rate of **5.99%** of net ordinary/business income, providing an offsetting credit to members.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/business-tax-forms/bank-deposits-bank-excise-insurance-public-service-and-surplus-lines
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax

### Individual Returns and Extensions
* **Calendar-Year Due Date:** Due on or before April 15 following the close of the tax year (or the next business day if April 15 falls on a weekend or holiday). Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Extension Rules:** 
  * Filing **Form RI-4868** provides an automatic six (6) month extension of time to file (to October 15). 
  * An extension extends the time to file, not the time to pay. 
  * To be valid, a "proper estimate" must be declared and at least eighty percent (80%) of the tax liability must be paid by the original April 15 deadline. 
  * If no Rhode Island tax payment is due and a federal extension was filed, taxpayers do not need to file Form RI-4868 separately; they attach federal Form 4868 upon filing the RI return.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/personal-income-tax-forms
  * https://tax.ri.gov/guidance/advisories/adv-2024-14
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/personal-income-tax

---

### Corporate and Pass-Through Return Due Dates and Extensions
* **Return Due Dates (Calendar-Year Filers):**
  * **C Corporations (Form RI-1120C):** Due on or before the 15th day of the fourth (4th) month following the close of the taxable year (April 15). Applies to TY 2025 and 2026.
  * **S Corporations (Form RI-1120S):** Due on or before the 15th day of the third (3rd) month following the close of the taxable year (March 15). Applies to TY 2025 and 2026.
  * **Partnerships / LLCs / LLPs / LPs (Form RI-1065):** Due on or before the 15th day of the third (3rd) month following the close of the taxable year (March 15).
  * **Single-Member LLCs (SMLLCs):** Disregarded SMLLCs owned by an individual (calendar-year) are due on the 15th day of the fourth (4th) month (April 15).
* **Extension Rules:**
  * Requested using **Form BUS-EXT** (Form RI-7004 was discontinued after tax year 2022).
  * Grants an automatic six (6) month extension of time to file (extends March 15 filers to September 15; extends April 15 filers to October 15). 
  * Extends time to file only, not to pay. Requires reasonable estimation and payment of full tax due or the minimum statutory fee/tax ($400).
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax/tax-filing-requirements
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/corporate-tax-forms
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax/pass-through-entities

---

### Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)
* **Existence & Statutory Authority:** Authorized under R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-11-2.3.
* **Rate:** 
  * Base rate of **5.99%**.
  * *Change:* Beginning in 2026 (State Fiscal Year 2027 budget), qualifying electing entities may additionally elect to pay the High-Income Surtax at the entity level in addition to the 5.99% rate.
* **Credit Percentage for Owners:** 
  * *Change:* For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025 (applies to TY 2025 and TY 2026), the owner's state tax credit is calculated at **90%** of the entity-level tax paid (reduced from 100% in prior years).
* **How and When to Elect:**
  * Elected annually by filing **RI Schedule PTE** with the entity's return (**Form RI-1065**, **Form RI-1120S**, or **Form RI-1041**) by the annual return due date, including extensions. The standalone Form RI-PTE was discontinued beginning with TY 2024.
  * Making the election relieves the entity of withholding requirements under R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-11-2.2 for electing members.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax/pass-through-entities
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/business-tax-forms/pass-through-entity-election-forms

---

### Composite / Group Nonresident Returns
* **Return Form & Rate:** Filed on **Form RI-1040C** (Composite Income Tax Return) at the highest personal income tax rate of **5.99%**.
* **Due Date:** Due on or before the fifteenth (15th) day of the third (3rd) month following the close of the entity's taxable year (March 15 for calendar-year entities; March 16, 2026, when March 15 falls on a Sunday).
* **Extensions:** An automatic six (6) month extension is available using **Form RI-4868C**.
* **Eligibility & Member Election:**
  * Available for nonresident members whose only source of Rhode Island income is from one or more pass-through entities.
  * Members must execute **Form RI-1040C-NE** (Nonresident Member Election) and submit it to the entity, which must keep the forms on file.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/business-tax-forms/pass-through-entity-withholding-and-composite-return-tax-forms
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax/pass-through-entities

---

### Estimated Taxes and Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Throughs
* **Nonresident Pass-Through Withholding (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-11-2.2):**
  * **Rates:** **5.99%** for individuals, trusts, partnerships, and S corporations; **7.0%** for C corporations.
  * **Reporting:** Reported on **RI Schedule PTW** attached directly to Form RI-1065, RI-1120S, or RI-1041 (the standalone Form RI-1096PT series was discontinued starting TY 2023/2024).
  * **Exceptions:** No withholding is required if a member's pro rata share of Rhode Island source income is less than $1,000; or the member participates in a composite filing (Form RI-1040C); or the entity makes the PTET election (RI Schedule PTE); or the entity is a publicly traded partnership under IRC § 7704(b).
* **Estimated Tax Payments:**
  * **Individuals:** Must file and pay estimated taxes using **Form RI-1040ES** if net tax liability can reasonably be expected to exceed credits/withholding by **$250 or more**. Due in four installments: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.
  * **Corporations & Pass-Throughs:** Corporations with estimated tax liability exceeding **$500** must pay quarterly installments (April 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15 for calendar filers) using **Form BUS-EST**. Pass-through entity withholding and PTET estimates are also remitted using **Form BUS-EST**.
  * **Composite Filers:** Estimated taxes are paid using **Form RI-1040C-ES**.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/tax-sections/corporate-tax/pass-through-entities
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/business-tax-forms/pass-through-entity-withholding-and-composite-return-tax-forms
  * https://rules.sos.ri.gov/regulations/part/280-20-25-5

---

### Main Return Forms (TY 2025 and 2026)
* **Individual:**
  * **Form RI-1040:** Resident Individual Income Tax Return.
  * **Form RI-1040NR:** Nonresident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Return.
* **Corporate:**
  * **Form RI-1120C:** Business Corporation Tax Return (applies to C corporations).
* **Pass-Through Entities:**
  * **Form RI-1120S:** Subchapter S Corporation Tax Return.
  * **Form RI-1065:** Partnership and Limited Liability Company Income Return.
  * **Form RI-1041:** Fiduciary Income Tax Return (Estates and Trusts).
  * **Form RI-1040C:** Composite Income Tax Return.
  * **Key Schedules:** **RI Schedule PTE** (Pass-Through Entity Election) and **RI Schedule PTW** (Pass-Through Withholding Transmittal Schedule), attached to Forms RI-1065, RI-1120S, and RI-1041.
* **Official URLs:**
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/personal-income-tax-forms
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/corporate-tax-forms
  * https://tax.ri.gov/forms/business-tax-forms/pass-through-entity-withholding-and-composite-return-tax-forms

proposals.value: Calendar-year S corporations and partnerships must file by March 15, while C corporations and individual single-member LLCs are due April 15. Form BUS-EXT provides an automatic six-month extension of time to file upon proper estimation and payment of any tax due.

Rhode Island allows an elective pass-through entity tax at a base rate of 5.99%, providing owners a state tax credit equal to 90% of the entity-level tax paid. The annual election is made by submitting RI Schedule PTE with the entity return by its due date, including extensions.

The elective pass-through entity tax is assessed at a 5.99% base rate with an additional High-Income Surtax entity-level election available beginning in 2026, granting owners a 90% tax credit. Entities elect annually by filing RI Schedule PTE alongside their return by the due date including extensions.

Pass-through entities may file a composite return for eligible nonresidents using Form RI-1040C at the highest personal rate of 5.99%, due on March 15 for calendar filers. An automatic six-month extension of time to file is available by filing Form RI-4868C.
